craft_claim: Expressionless delivery is only the surface half of deadpan; if the content is not absurd, incongruous, or loaded, the flatness produces confusion or blandness instead of comedy — the tone fails when the gap closes from the content side.

supporting_evidence.note: With no salient non-literal target in the content, the literal-first pathway terminates at sincerity: the reader has nowhere to redirect to, so the flat sentence simply states. Tier 2; explains the mechanism of the failure.

If there is no attitude being echoed and dissociated (nothing in the content worth dissociating from), the echoic account predicts no ironic interpretation arises. Tier 2; the theory's own negative case doubles as the failure diagnostic.

The lexical definition fixes only the *face*, never the content — which is exactly why practitioners import the word to mean neutral or bland writing and lose the comic engine. Tier 5; corroborates the confusion at the vocabulary level, never sole support.

counterevidence.location: discussion of ironic reward on rereading
counterevidence.note: Booth argues sustained ironic passages repay rereading, so a passage that reads flat the first time may reveal its irony to a patient or primed reader. Mitigates but does not defeat: reliance on rereading is a poor bet for one-pass prose, and the card should assume single-pass reading.

scope: All deadpan prose; the check applies before any use of the tone. Distinct from failure mode 2 (missing key) — here the key may exist but points at nothing, because the content is ordinary.
exceptions: In satire framed by an explicit container (a named target, a genre promise of satire), flatness of content can be temporary: the loaded element may arrive late, provided it arrives.
